findings.title: Exclude raw identifiers from nested-owner keyword detection
findings.detail: The rewrite scanner splits r#impl into r, # and impl, then treats impl as an owner keyword without checking its raw-identifier prefix. For an ordinary struct literal named r#impl, nested_owner_end accepts its opening brace as an owner body even though no owner is declared. Consequently outer Self inside the initializer is skipped. A concrete public-path input is: struct Tax; struct Order(u64); struct r#impl { n: usize } followed by impl Order { fn f() -> usize { let value = r#impl { n: std::mem::size_of::<Self>() }; value.n } } and fn main() { println!("{}", Order::f()); }. Moving Order::f to Tax through move_associated_function leaves size_of::<Self>() in that initializer while moving its enclosing function into impl Tax. The source-derived result is a silent 8-to-0 change on the recorded x86_64 platform, with valid source on both sides. The owner guard also skips the same literal outside a macro, so it does not refuse the move; normal and forced application share the rewrite. The repair of raw r#fn in type_header does not reach these owner-keyword decisions.
findings.evidence: Source-derived public-path trace, not executed by this reviewer: associated.rs:59-76 selects the ordinary outer impl; associated.rs:115 calls ensure_owner_context; syntax.rs:173-184 passes raw status only to MacroContext and still skips the raw identifier's brace span; syntax.rs:99-107 repeats the unguarded owner decision during rewriting; syntax.rs:241 returns owner_body_end for the struct literal; associated.rs:231-235 inserts swap_names output, and associated.rs:251-259 permits application when diagnostics/unmatched are empty. signature/call_sites.rs:117-123 explicitly returns no opaque token for r#impl because no quote follows the hashes. context.rs:41-44 already distinguishes raw fn for header tracking. The retained raw-identifier control tests only a field named r#fn (tests/rust_method_preservation/owner_header_regressions.rs:14-19), not a raw owner-keyword type expression.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry raw-identifier identity into the owner-keyword decisions in swap_names, ensure_owner_context and ensure_capture_identity, so r#impl/r#trait/r#mod cannot introduce owner spans. Preserve the existing ordinary nested-owner and macro ambiguity behavior; verify this specific public move without changing literal bytes or broadly refusing raw identifiers.

findings.title: Keep array-length operators out of nested-owner generic matching
findings.detail: nested_owner_end still pushes a generic closer for every '<', including shift operators in an array length. A concrete public associated move can have the following body in impl Order, where Order(u64) moves f to unit Tax: struct Inner<T>(std::marker::PhantomData<T>); impl Inner<[u8; 1 << 2]> { fn size() -> usize { std::mem::size_of::<Self>() } } std::mem::size_of::<Self>() + Inner::<[u8; 4]>::size(). Matching the nested impl pushes '>' for its generic argument, ']' for the array, then two more '>' entries for '<<'. At ']' the top no longer matches, so line 258 returns None and the genuine owner's body is scanned as the outer scope. Its Self becomes Order. The source-derived expected transformation therefore changes output from 8 to 16 on the recorded x86_64 platform while still compiling, and the same unchecked rewrite is used in normal and forced application. The latest array-length repair updates type_header, but nested_owner_end has its own delimiter stack and does not use that expression-state correction.
findings.evidence: Source-derived public-path trace, not an observed new runtime result: associated.rs:115 validates ownership with syntax.rs:175-177; syntax.rs:250-258 loses the nested impl at the array closer; syntax.rs:102-107 consequently does not skip the genuine nested owner when rewriting; associated.rs:234 applies the Self map, with normal/force write gate at associated.rs:254. context.rs:67-73 and 87-90 handle direct array semicolons only in type_header. The recorded new array fixtures are helper return types (tests/rust_method_preservation/owner_header_regressions.rs:23-29); the existing nested-owner const matrix uses braced const arguments (same file:73-97), which takes the separate skip at syntax.rs:245-248. The retained owner type-macro controls at tests/rust_method_preservation/owner_boundary_regressions.rs:55-66 exercise macro token trees, not this direct array-length expression.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the nested-owner header scan the same bounded array type-versus-length distinction already present in type_header. A direct semicolon in a square-bracket frame must enter length-expression context until the matching bracket, so shifts/comparisons cannot corrupt the enclosing generic stack. Verify the specific nested impl move while retaining the independent owner's Self.
